WELCOME, OBSERVER

A world to explore. A life to build.

Choose Play as a citizen in the lobby to walk with WASD or arrows. Turn with Q/E or right-drag, and use F or the activity buttons to interact. Work earns money; helping and meeting neighbors builds social credit. Buy meals, rest, and rent a home. Observer mode gives you city-building tools.

Choose City Stories for cozy building and community challenges, or Chaos Lab for survival and experiments. Both modes keep your current city. Challenges add goals, construction grants, and saved medals. Free play has unlimited environmental tools. Open the lobby any time from the mode button.

Watch 50 citizens work, trade, form relationships, elect leaders, and raise families. Click a person or choose one from Citizens to inspect their needs, memories, and changing motivations.

Drag to move across town. Use WASD or arrow keys, or click the minimap to travel. Scroll or use +/− to zoom. Right-drag or Q/E rotates. Follow a citizen from their journal. Space pauses time. Time advances while the page is open; your world saves to your shared username every 30 seconds and when you log out. At 20×, generations evolve faster.

Environment is your sandbox: place facilities, landscape lots, close or reopen road junctions, create temporary hazards, and change weather, power, fertility, temperature, or daylight. Select a tool and click the map. Undo reverses your last map edit. Citizens choose destinations and actions independently.

Each citizen has a fruit-fly-inspired associative learning model: 20 inputs, 32 projection neurons, 128 sparsely active memory cells, 16 recurrent context cells, and 8 actions. Rewards from completed activities change memory weights; every eight outcomes consolidate long-term lessons. This is a simplified game model, not a biological fly brain or conscious AI. Activity and thought summaries explain simulation state. Citizen minds are included in cloud saves, with browser backups and file exports. Previous memories and neural weights are preserved during migration.
